facts.text: README describes the repository as a Sim2Sim pipeline for RL quadruped policies in ROS 2 Gazebo.
README says the stack is tested on ROS 2 Humble and Ubuntu 22.04.
README lists the Gazebo launch, three policy controller executables and the UI executable.
README says the UI controls the robot's command_velocity interactively.
DreamWaQ creates a PoseStamped subscription on /robot_velocity_command with queue depth 10.
DreamWaQ imports PoseStamped from geometry_msgs.msg.
DreamWaQ's velocity callback copies pose.position x, y and z into the command vector.
DreamWaQ creates Float64MultiArray publishers on /joint_effort_controller/commands and /policy.
DreamWaQ subscribes to Imu on /imu_plugin/out and JointState on /joint_states.
DreamWaQ imports Imu and JointState from sensor_msgs.msg.
DreamWaQ's joint-state callback requires at least 12 positions and reorders 12 indices; the controller does not verify the attached joint names.
DreamWaQ runs a 0.005 s timer and its comment labels the policy dt 0.02 and the PD controller dt 0.005.
HIM's command callback comment names x, y and yaw.
HIM's observation builder comments the three command scales as lin_vel, lin_vel and ang_vel.
Walk-These-Ways creates the same PoseStamped, Imu, JointState, effort publisher and timer interface.
Walk-These-Ways clips policy actions to 10, scales by 0.25, reduces hip entries by 0.5 and uses proportional 20 and derivative 0.5 gains.
HIM clips the computed torque command to -80 and 80.
The Gazebo controller manager runs at 1000 Hz and declares a joint_state_broadcaster plus an effort_controllers/JointGroupEffortController.
The effort controller lists the FL, FR, RL and RR hip, thigh and calf joints and uses the effort command interface.
The Gazebo launch enables use_sim_time and spawns entity go1 at z 0.4.
The URDF declares the FR hip joint as revolute with effort 23.7, lower -0.863, upper 0.863 and velocity 30.1.
The URDF declares the FR calf joint as revolute with effort 35.55, lower -2.818, upper -0.888 and velocity 20.06.
README's Real Robot Integration section is still 'Coming soon...'.
DreamWaQ starts with the command vector 0.15, 0.0, 0.0.
DreamWaQ's control loop runs the policy every fourth tick, then computes PD torques toward the policy's joint targets and publishes them on every tick.
The README starts the Gazebo simulation with ros2 launch and each policy controller with ros2 run and no argument.
The Gazebo launch includes gazebo_ros's gazebo.launch.py.
gzserver.launch.py adds the init and factory gazebo_ros system plugins to the server command.
gzserver.launch.py defaults its init and factory arguments to true.
The init plugin takes the shared gazebo_ros node from gazebo_ros::Node::Get().
gazebo_ros::Node::Get creates the shared node named gazebo with an empty namespace.
The gazebo_ros executor spins its nodes on a thread of its own.
The init plugin creates the pause_physics and unpause_physics services with the std_srvs::srv::Empty type.
OnPause calls world_->SetPaused(true).
OnUnpause calls world_->SetPaused(false).
The init plugin publishes the simulation clock from a world-update-begin callback.
The factory plugin creates the get_model_list service with the gazebo_msgs::srv::GetModelList type.
GetModelList sets header.stamp to the world's simulation time, lists the model names and sets success true.
The GetModelList response documents header.stamp as the simulation time when the data was collected.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.
gazebo_ros2_control spins its controller manager's executor on a thread of its own.
gazebo_ros2_control connects its Update to the world-update begin event.
gazebo_ros2_control's Update reads the simulation time, updates the controllers and writes their commands to the joints.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned observations and a publication recorder; no physics step, wall-clock pacing, policy inference or trajectory replay

fidelity.engine: synthetic:ROS-free protocol fake (no Gazebo, no policy controller)
gaps: the fake answers the declared ROS endpoints only; it runs no Gazebo world, physics, contacts, IMU plugin, joint-state broadcaster, policy controller or ROS graph
the fake's IMU and joint-state samples are placeholders and are not integrated with the velocity publication; a live run must supply the operator's Gazebo and controller processes
the fake's publication receipt proves only that rosbridge accepted the PoseStamped, not that a controller consumed it, that the robot moved or that it stopped

the pinned nodes expose no stop, pause or reset service and no action interface; the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause, confirmed by the E1 stall read-back: the fake keeps a paused flag that /pause_physics sets and a sim-time stamp that /get_model_list reports and that advances on every answer unless paused; it runs no Gazebo World::Step

a frozen get_model_list stamp is also what a hung but unpaused gzserver shows (nothing advances then either); a GUI step or a WorldControl multi_step between the two samples fails the check (fails closed); the e-stop declares estop_latency_ms 1500 because the pause (400 ms), two read-backs (300 ms each) and the 250 ms interval exceed the default 1000 ms budget

no unpause is offered: the policy node stores the last setpoint (initially 0.15, load_dreamwaq_policy.py:167) and publishes joint efforts every 5 ms (lines 182, 230-270); started with ros2 run and no parameter (README.md:86-90) its timer runs on the system clock through the pause on stale joint and IMU samples, so the package cannot clear what the legs do on an unpause; the operator recovers outside MHS (stop the policy node, then the Gazebo GUI play button or ros2 service call /unpause_physics)

while paused, /joint_states (joint_state_broadcaster through gazebo_ros2_control), /imu_plugin/out and /clock come only from world updates, so the joint-state and IMU reads fail NOT_READY after their timeouts (the fake silences them while its flag is set)

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI, a WorldControl message or any ROS 2 client of /unpause_physics; MHS does not watch the sim time after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)
the deployment's gazebo_ros, gazebo_ros2_control and Gazebo must be the pinned 3.9.0, 0.4.12 and 11.15.1 releases the companion citations name; rosbridge cannot read their versions
the clone supports three alternative policy controllers and hard-coded checkpoint paths; this package binds the common topic interface, not a particular policy, checkpoint or launch namespace
the clone's Real Robot Integration is not implemented, so no hardware interface is claimed

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused: two get_model_list answers 250 ms apart carried the same sim time, so no world update runs and gazebo_ros2_control applies no joint effort; it is a frozen sim time, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: an operator stops the policy node, then unpauses outside MHS.
